maximum_gap.optimal:
n = size of nums; if n < 2: return 0
lo = min of nums, hi = max of nums
width = max(1, (hi - lo) // (n - 1))   (the max gap is at least the average gap, so it never sits inside a bucket)
count = (hi - lo) // width + 1
bucket_min, bucket_max = count empty slots each
for each x in nums:
    b = (x - lo) // width
    if bucket_min[b] is empty or x < bucket_min[b]: bucket_min[b] = x
    if bucket_max[b] is empty or x > bucket_max[b]: bucket_max[b] = x
best = 0, prev_max = lo
for each bucket b in order:
    if bucket b is empty: skip   (the gap spans it)
    best = max(best, bucket_min[b] - prev_max)
    prev_max = bucket_max[b]
return best

contains_duplicate_iii.optimal:
width = value_diff + 1   (two values in the same bucket differ by at most value_diff)
buckets = dict bucket id -> the single value stored in it
for each index i with value x:
    b = floor(x / width)
    if b is in buckets: return true
    for each neighbour in (b - 1, b + 1):   (close values can only be in adjacent buckets)
        if neighbour is in buckets and |buckets[neighbour] - x| <= value_diff: return true
    buckets[b] = x
    if i >= index_diff:   (keep only the last index_diff indices)
        old = nums[i - index_diff]
        remove bucket floor(old / width)
return false

reverse_pairs.optimal:
merge(left, right): the usual two-finger merge of two sorted lists
sort_and_count(arr):   (returns arr sorted and the number of reverse pairs inside it)
    if size of arr <= 1: return arr, 0
    mid = size of arr // 2
    left, count_left = sort_and_count(first half)
    right, count_right = sort_and_count(second half)
    count = count_left + count_right
    j = 0   (right[0..j) are exactly the r with 2r < x)
    for each x in left:   (x increases, so j never moves back)
        while j < size of right and 2 * right[j] < x:
            j += 1
        count += j
    return merge(left, right), count
return the count from sort_and_count(nums)

create_sorted_array_through_instructions.optimal:
fenwick_add(i): while i < size of tree: tree[i] += 1, i += lowest set bit of i
fenwick_prefix(i): total = 0; while i > 0: total += tree[i], i -= lowest set bit of i; return total
size = max of instructions
tree = size + 1 zeros   (1-indexed: tree[i] covers the values (i - lowbit(i), i])
cost = 0, inserted = 0
for each x in instructions:
    less = fenwick_prefix(x - 1)
    greater = inserted - fenwick_prefix(x)   (all inserted so far minus those <= x)
    cost += min(less, greater)
    fenwick_add(x)
    inserted += 1
return cost mod 1e9+7

trapping_rain_water.optimal:
left = 0, right = n - 1
left_max = 0, right_max = 0, water = 0
while left < right:
    if height[left] < height[right]:   (the right side has a taller bar, so left_max alone sets the level)
        left_max = max(left_max, height[left])
        water += left_max - height[left]
        left += 1
    else:
        right_max = max(right_max, height[right])
        water += right_max - height[right]
        right -= 1
return water

reverse_nodes_in_k_group.optimal:
dummy = new node pointing at head
group_prev = dummy   (the node just before the current block)
loop forever:
    kth = group_prev
    advance kth k times; if it runs off the end: return dummy.next   (fewer than k left, leave them)
    after = kth.next   (first node after the block)
    prev = after, cur = group_prev.next   (the reversed block's tail must point to after)
    while cur is not after:   (the usual three-pointer reversal, stopped at the block end)
        nxt = cur.next, cur.next = prev, prev = cur, cur = nxt
    old_head = group_prev.next   (the old block head is now the block tail)
    group_prev.next = kth
    group_prev = old_head

number_of_valid_words_for_each_puzzle.optimal:
letter_mask(text) = 26-bit mask with one bit per letter in text
counts = dict mask -> how many words have exactly that letter set
for each word: counts[letter_mask(word)] += 1
answer = empty list
for each puzzle:
    full = letter_mask(puzzle), first = bit of puzzle[0], total = 0
    sub = full
    loop:   (visit every submask of full, from full down to 0)
        if sub contains first: total += counts[sub]   (the word must contain the first letter)
        if sub == 0: stop
        sub = (sub - 1) AND full   (the next smaller submask of full)
    append total to answer
return answer
